slides.teacher_cue: New sound. Tongue rises toward the hard palate without touching it. Air flows freely. Voice on. This is y at the START of a word before a vowel — consonant y. Korean has the same sound: 야 (ya), 여 (yeo). It is the most accessible y sound for Korean learners. Important: y has four different sounds in English — this is the first one. Today: y at the start of a word.
slides.expected_response: Students produce consonant /j/ cleanly and understand that y is a consonant here, not a vowel.
slides.correction_move: Model y-es, y-et, y-ell. Students copy. Explain that y here is a consonant — it makes a sound before the vowel, just like s or t.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students treating y as a vowel and trying to blend it as a vowel sound. Redirect — consonant y slides quickly into the following vowel.
